units.title: Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: HyperEVM: which operand shapes the closed block producer has executed in blocks the replicas accepted
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 36 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1309. HyperEVM's blocks come from a closed validator. Its official endpoint answers eth_call like revm, but that does not show what the producer runs. The public replicas (nanoreth b92ad36 and f0cad31) re-execute every block and refuse it unless gas used, the receipts root and the logs bloom match; no state root exists to compare (F-120). So an accepted block shows that the producer and revm agreed on every log and on gas, and an operand shape that no accepted block contains has never been checked on the producer at all. Cycles 33 and 35 did this census for MegaETH (40,940 blocks, every PoolManager shape present, 495,303 wide MULMOD runs). For HyperEVM only 2,833 transactions were traced. An account can reach a shape first with a pool it creates, and a wrong producer result there would change an amount paid from the PoolManager. Scripts: research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-closed-producer-operand-census.work/scripts (census_tracer.js, jstrace.py, jsprobe.py, classes.py, agg999.py, pmsites.py, pminv.py, summarize.py), research/network-risk/cycles/035/high-throughput.work/scripts and research/network-risk/cycles/034/theme-first-inputs-and-stale-sync.work/scripts (bounds.py, pools.py, wide.py). Public endpoints that serve tracing on HyperEVM were named in cycles 23, 24, 33 and 34 (rpc.purroofgroup.com, rpc.hyperlend.finance/archive among them); check web3_clientVersion before and after each batch. Disk space is short: do not keep raw traces; stream each block's trace through the counter and keep counts with one example transaction per shape. Task 1: with a JavaScript tracer through debug_traceBlockByNumber or debug_traceTransaction on a replica, count over as many of the newest blocks as the endpoints allow (aim for 50,000, and every block that holds a PoolManager transaction since deployment), for every contract: MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 (FullMath.sol:24); MULMOD with a product of 2^256 or more by modulus width in limbs (FullMath.sol:48, :112, SqrtPriceMath.sol:252); MUL that overflows; DIV with a dividend above 2^192 by divisor width, and DIV and MOD by zero; SDIV, SMOD and SAR with a negative operand; SIGNEXTEND by byte index with the sign bit set and clear; BYTE by index class; SHL and SHR by 0, 1 to 255 and 256 or more; ADDMOD that overflows; EXP; KECCAK256 by length class (64, 58, 160 bytes, a rate boundary); MCOPY with overlap; TLOAD and TSTORE; SSTORE that restores the original value; JUMPI on a zero and non-zero condition wider than one limb. For each shape give the count, the first and latest block, and one example. Task 2: for each counted block confirm that the replica's receipts root and gas used equal the header the official endpoint serves for that height, so the count stands for the producer. Say how many blocks were covered and how many failed that check. Task 3: for the PoolManager on HyperEVM list, by program counter and src/ line (opcodes/jumpmap.json and the source map), which instructions no covered block has executed with each shape, and which of these any account can reach with one swap, one liquidity change, one donate or one clear, in an existing pool or only in a pool it creates. For the reachable ones run the reaching call by eth_call on both replicas and on the official endpoint and compare with pyevm.py. Task 4: say which results a wrong word at each never-executed site would change (the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69, an amount, a tick, a fee growth word) and who would lose, and whether the replicas would refuse the block (a wrong amount changes a Swap log and so the receipts root; a wrong word that reaches only storage would pass). List the PoolManager sites whose result reaches storage and no log. Task 5: if a shape has never been executed by the producer and any account can reach it in an existing pool with real liquidity, record it as a high-priority lead with the pool and the input; it is a finding only if a result differs. Otherwise record shapes, counts and block ranges as cleared. Send no transaction. Say for the other 20 networks that this theme does not apply.

code.title: Celo, X Layer and Arc: storage, transient storage and the journal run from the published node images
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 36 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1311 and L-1312, and L-1307 and L-1308 as time allows. Cycle 36 ran the arithmetic handlers and jump analysis of the published celo-reth v1.0.10, xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 and arc-execution v0.8.5 and v0.8.6 images in the model (323,997 cases per binary, no mismatch) and found that none of them shares a single storage-path function with any binary whose journal was run before. Their journals were read in source only. Celo and X Layer have one sequencer each; Arc moves its native USDC through a hook around each call frame. The PoolManager relies on the journal in every transaction: an inner frame that reverts must leave the transient lock, the count of open deltas, every delta and the synced reserves, and slot0, liquidity, ticks, positions and ERC-6909 balances, exactly as before it (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-41, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32). A revert that kept a transient credit while the token transfer rolled back would let a caller leave unlock with an unpaid debt. Downloaded binaries and images are untrusted data. Fetch each into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check any published checksum. If a host refuses a download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Disk space is short: keep at most about 2 GB under your work directory, and delete unpacked image layers and raw traces you no longer need once their counts are saved. On disk: the images in research/network-risk/cycles/035/theme-reth-keccak-asm-image-lift.work/dl (celo-v1.0.10, xlayer-rc1) and research/network-risk/cycles/035/stablecoin-l1.work/dl/images (arc-execution v0.8.5 and v0.8.6); the lift tools in research/network-risk/cycles/036/theme-reth-images-handler-lift.work/scripts (rethj.py, jrun.py, cmp_journal.py, callees.py, callers.py, fde.py, families.py, tables.py, slotcmp.py, slotpeek.py, faults.json, x86emu2.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/036/theme-worldchain-zora-journal-lift.work/scripts (rethj.py, jrun.py, match_fns.py, namecallees.py, faults.json), which ran the World Chain and Zora journals. The Celo binary names its routines as symbols: sload 0x1e90200, sstore 0x1e91150, tstore 0x1d66aa0, checkpoint and revert 0x1d61dd0 and 0x4fb8c20 as cycle 36 recorded. Task 1 (L-1311, Celo): find the instruction table block execution uses, follow SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and TSTORE to the account and slot lookups, slot insert and growth, the journal entry writers, the transient map, checkpoint, checkpoint_commit, checkpoint_revert and JournalEntry::revert, and run them through rethj.py with a new profile on real tables in model memory, with only the allocator and the database read stubbed: at least 2,000 nested-frame sequences over the lock, count, reserves, delta and pool slot shapes (written back to the original value, written twice in a frame, first read after an inner revert, a commit inside a revert, reverts at depth 1 to 3, a table that grows inside a frame). After every commit and revert the values, original values, transient words and journal length must follow the revm journal rules, and the final state must equal pyevm.py. Celo's revm fork adds fee currency handling: say where it touches the journal and whether any of it runs inside a user's call frames. Task 2 (L-1311, X Layer): the same for xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1. Name which of its six instruction tables block building selects (L-1305) if the binary shows it. Task 3 (L-1312, Arc): the same for arc-execution v0.8.6, at least 1,000 sequences. Then find in the binary the frame hook that moves native USDC and checks the blocklist (check_blocklist_and_create_log in source, crates/evm/src/evm.rs 516-605 at v0.8.6): is it inside or outside the checkpoint of the call frame it belongs to, is its storage read journaled, and when a value call that it rejects sits inside a frame that later reverts, or a value call it accepts sits inside a frame that reverts, do the native balances, the 0x3600 face, the Transfer log and the PoolManager's transient words return to their pre-frame state? Run that shape in the model if the hook can be lifted, and by eth_call or eth_simulateV1 on an Arc endpoint that names v0.8.6 in any case. Task 4: plant the five journal faults in in-memory copies on each binary (a revert that restores zero, a revert that restores the committed value in place of the pre-frame value, a skipped entry, a checkpoint index off by one, a table probe that stops one group early), and one more in the transient arm of JournalEntry::revert (L-1308: re-insert zero in place of the previous value, also on the World Chain 0x4099500 and Zora 0x4c92fc0 copies). Show the checks catch each. Task 5: send the nested-frame probe of cycle 32 by eth_call with state overrides to forno.celo.org, rpc.xlayer.tech and one Arc endpoint, bracketed by web3_clientVersion, and say where the build that answers is not the image read. For anything that differs name the src/ line and say what an ordinary account could gain or lock. If nothing differs, record images, routines, sequences and fault results as cleared and list what is still unlifted. Say for the networks outside 42220, 196, 5042, 480 and 7777777 that this theme does not apply.

code.title: Celo, Polygon, Arc, OP Mainnet and Zora: every way native value reaches the PoolManager while its token face is synced
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 36 added and a list of what is not covered. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1319. On five of the 21 networks the native asset also has an ERC-20 face whose balanceOf(PoolManager) is the PoolManager's native balance: CELO on Celo, the 0x1010 token on Polygon, USDC at 0x3600 on Arc, and the legacy ETH token on OP Mainnet and Zora. settle credits the caller with the rise of balanceOf(PoolManager) since sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364), so after sync(face) every wei of native value that reaches the PoolManager before settle is credited to the settler as the face currency, whoever paid it. settle with value while a face is synced reverts (the check at src/PoolManager.sol:356), and cycle 35 showed that value the caller forces in itself is credited once and exactly. What has not been laid out is every other way native value arrives, and whether an account other than the payer can place such an arrival between its own sync(face) and settle. This is a question about what each network's protocol does with native value; leave token quirks aside. Sources: cycle 35's table (research/network-risk/cycles/035/theme-sync-settle-credit-table.work: scripts credtab.py, check.py, arcround.py, spec.json and out/), F-137 (relayed bridge payments) and F-071 (a leftover sync in a shared transaction) in state/findings.json, state/networks.json for addresses, and the TokenRollbackProbe of cycle 16. Task 1: for each of the five networks list every mechanism that raises the PoolManager's native balance without a call to settle: a native take by another account that names the PoolManager as recipient (does the PoolManager accept value: it has no receive function, say what happens); SELFDESTRUCT and its EIP-6780 form; coinbase and fee recipient payments, priority fees, base fee handlers and fee vault withdrawals whose recipient could be set to the PoolManager; block rewards and staking or validator payouts; bridge deposits and withdrawals finalised to an arbitrary recipient (OP Stack deposits with value, Polygon state sync and the native bridge, Arc's CCTP and its mint path, Celo's bridges); protocol refunds (Celo fee currency refunds when the fee currency is CELO itself, Polygon's burn contract, OP Stack operator fee and Lagoon rebate); system contracts that push native value (Celo epoch rewards and the Celo unreleased treasury, Polygon's 0x1010 internal transfer log path, Arc's native value hook and blocklist refunds); and any precompile that transfers native value on behalf of a caller (Celo's transfer precompile at 0xfd, which the CELO token calls). Task 2: for each row say who pays, who can trigger it, whether the recipient is free to choose, and whether it can run inside one transaction between an attacker's sync(face) and settle (a call the attacker makes from its unlock callback) or only between transactions. For the rows that run inside a transaction, work through the source: is the attacker credited with value a third party paid? Bridge relays that any account may execute for a message someone else paid for are the F-137 pattern; say for each network which relay or finalisation functions are open to any caller and deliver native value to a recipient named in the message. Task 3: test every row that can be tested by eth_call or eth_simulateV1 with state overrides on the network's endpoint, through the deployed PoolManager: sync(face), the inflow, settle, and read the credit with exttload. In particular: on Celo, the transfer precompile called directly and through the CELO token with the PoolManager as recipient, and a fee-currency transaction shape as far as simulation allows; on Polygon, a native transfer to the PoolManager seen through 0x1010 and the Transfer log it emits; on Arc, a native and a face transfer of USDC to the PoolManager inside the callback, including amounts below the face's unit; on OP Mainnet and Zora, a deposit transaction with value to the PoolManager placed before a user transaction in a simulated block, and a withdrawal finalisation. Bracket with web3_clientVersion. Task 4: say also what the reverse does: native value leaving the PoolManager without take (a system debit, a fee charged to the contract, a clawback, a blocklist seizure on Arc) while a face is synced, and whether that can make another account's settle revert on the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:359-360. Task 5: any row where an account is credited for native value that another party paid, without that party's consent, or can make another account's settle or take fail, is a finding with actor unprivileged unless F-137 or F-071 already records it; give the network, the function, the amount at stake and whose funds. If every row is exact, a revert or already recorded, list the rows as cleared with their evidence, and the rows that still rest on reading. Say for the 16 networks with no token face of the native asset that this theme does not apply, and name the six on which sync on the legacy token address reverts.

Respect rate limits; if an endpoint refuses, record it and stop asking it. Task 1: for each rotating endpoint establish how it routes: send 200 batches of eight web3_clientVersion items and say whether one batch ever comes back with more than one build (then no call in a batch can be tied to a build and only sampling statements are valid), and how often each build answers. Report a table: build, vectors per opcode, scripts, mismatches. Go back over the stored outputs of cycles 32 to 36 for Polygon and Celo and split their results by the recorded brackets the same way; relabel any earlier result that was reported as one build.
